correctness.rationale: The central sign reduction and density integral are correct, but the frozen Finding literally asserts the satisfying set for a non-strict inequality as a union of open intervals and omits the transition slice. For example x=1, y=r_A(1)=3 gives product zero and satisfies the inequality but belongs to neither claimed open interval. Both endpoints must be included on each side of x_0; at x=x_0 the two middle roots coincide and the satisfying set is the entire closed interval [c_-,r_A]. The discrepancy has zero measure. The product of the three tangent factors has denominator (1+x²)^2(1+y²)^2; the roots satisfy c_-<r_B<r_A and c_-<c_+<r_A, with the only crossing r_B=c_+ at x²=3/5. On a fundamental square, the irrational flow gives Haar measure and independent Cauchy tangents; boundary sets have measure zero. The arctangent sum and difference identities (c_-c_+=-3, c_-+c_+=-4x) give the stated angular lengths. The same density applies to the energy-scale probability by weighting momentum by 2k and integrating by parts; this concerns the leading band condition, not exact finite-k band edges. Independent replay: /workspace/branches/8e755b8b-4247-4184-b173-46fdbd204ee7/independent_integral.py gives 0.639080422792130 by adaptive quadrature in x and after x=tan t; these error estimates are not rigorous enclosures. The source's 0.639081 is a close numerical approximation rather than the nearest six-decimal rounding. Frozen verify.py and VERIFICATION.md were inspected, not executed. Closing the intervals would not remove the decisive originality failure.
